name: Video inference: frame sampling and per-frame token cost
arithmetic_intensity: Video inference cost = frame_sampling_rate * tokens_per_frame * num_frames. For a 1-minute video at 1 fps = 60 frames. At 448x448 per frame with 2x2 spatial merge = 256 tokens per frame. Total visual tokens = 60*256 = 15,360. LLM prefill cost = 2*7e9*15,360 = 215 TFLOPs. KV cache cost = 15,360 * 57,344 B/token = 881 MB. For a 5-minute video at 2 fps = 600 frames = 153,600 visual tokens = 8.6 GB KV cache. Video blows up both prefill and KV cache because frame count multiplies the per-frame cost.
scales_with: tokens_per_frame (linear - depends on resolution and spatial merge)
workarounds: Reduce frame sampling rate - 0.5 fps instead of 1 fps halves cost
Use keyframe sampling - only sample frames with significant visual change
Use temporal pooling - pool adjacent frames before LLM
Use Perceiver/Q-Former per frame - compress each frame to 32-64 tokens
Use video-specific encoders (VideoMAE, TimeSformer) that process multiple frames jointly
notes: VIDEO INFERENCE COST: Video is the most expensive multimodal input because frame count multiplies the per-frame cost. A 1-minute video at 1 fps = 60 frames. At 448x448 per frame with 2x2 spatial merge (Qwen2-VL style) = 256 tokens per frame. Total visual tokens = 60*256 = 15,360. This is 15x a typical 1000-token text prompt. LLM prefill cost = 2*7e9*15,360 = 215 TFLOPs, which is 15x the cost of a 1000-token text prompt. KV cache cost = 15,360 * 57,344 B/token = 881 MB for a 7B model. For a 5-minute video at 2 fps = 600 frames = 153,600 visual tokens = 8.6 GB KV cache. The frame sampling rate is the primary cost knob: halving the rate halves the cost. LLaVA-NeXT-Video uses 1 fps sampling. Pixtral uses variable frame sampling based on video duration. The token counts are derived from the model configs; the FLOP and KV cache formulas are standard.
